chunks: The calamitous oath (al-yameen al-ghamus) that necessitates the Fire is (when) the man swears (an oath) against the right of a Muslim person, concerning the withholding of his wealth.

key_terms.الْيَمِينُ الْغَمُوسُ: The calamitous/plunging oath — an oath sworn deliberately to usurp another's rights; so called because it plunges its swearer into sin and Hellfire
key_terms.حَبْسِ مَالِهِ: Withholding/seizing his wealth — denying a person their lawful financial entitlement through a false oath

ai.seo_question: What is the calamitous oath (yameen ghamus) that leads to Hellfire in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the 'calamitous oath' (al-yameen al-ghamus) — an oath so grave it plunges its swearer into Hellfire. This particular oath involves falsely swearing to deny a Muslim his legitimate financial rights, thereby unjustly seizing or withholding his property. In classical Islamic jurisprudence, al-yameen al-ghamus refers specifically to a deliberate false oath used to usurp someone's rights, and this hadith clarifies its most egregious form: swearing falsely to deny a fellow Muslim's lawful financial claim.
